text:
Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating this 24-year-old male who has been followed for chronic infections since early childhood, with initial presentation around age three. He works as an office administrator, lives with his partner, and has a non-contributory family history without early childhood deaths or recurrent disease.

Over the years, he has suffered from persistent, intensely pruritic skin and frequent relapses of oral thrush. Examination of his digits reveals marked dystrophy across both fingernails and toenails. More recently, he developed an invasive deep dermatophytic soft-tissue infection of the left forearm, as well as a non-healing cutaneous ulcer on his lower extremity. Because of his recurrent fungal history, a lumbar puncture was previously performed following an episode of headache, which successfully excluded fungal meningitis; his CSF was sterile.

Recent laboratory investigations are notable for persistent peripheral lymphopenia accompanied by elevated total eosinophil counts. Quantitative immunoglobulins demonstrated raised serum IgG titers alongside a markedly increased IgE concentration. T-cell immunophenotyping confirmed that his total absolute CD8+ T-cell count is completely normal, and CD4+ T-helper subset proportions were likewise normal. Routine chemistries, including renal function and hepatic panels, have remained unremarkable. He currently takes daily cetirizine and uses bland emollients. 

I would be grateful for your assessment of his condition and any further management recommendations.

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Vance
